narrationTexts: I'll start by looking at what's in the working directory.
The PR sheet stops at 2026-06-17 — let me read the full commit log, which likely covers more.
finalText:
380 commits since 4.1. Here's the breakdown by type:

| type | count |
|---|---|
| chore | 153 |
| refactor | 73 |
| test | 64 |
| ci | 33 |
| **fix** | **26** |
| docs | 20 |
| **perf** | **10** |
| **feat** | **1** |

So ~37 commits out of 380 can possibly matter to a user, and several of those collapse into each other — the same bug class was fixed in 3–5 modules with an identical commit subject.

**Use `commits.log` as your source, not the PR sheet.** The sheet has 127 rows against 380 commits, it contains literal duplicate rows (`bump pino 9.2.0→9.3.1` appears 6 times), and where they overlap they disagree: the webhooks feature is Ana Ruiz in the log (`395fb48`) and Lena Fischer in the sheet (`#4191`). Check attribution before you credit anyone.

## What actually changed

**One new feature.** `feat(webhooks): retry failed deliveries with exponential backoff` (`395fb48`) — touches `src/webhooks/dispatch.js` *and* `src/core/config.js`, so it almost certainly added a config knob. Get the option name and defaults from whoever wrote it; that's the one thing in this release people need docs for.

**Fixes, deduplicated** (the parenthetical is how many modules got the same fix):

- Null cursor in the paginator no longer throws — queue, api, webhooks, db (4)
- Duplicate header no longer sent — core ×3, billing, http (5)
- Empty allowlist is handled instead of erroring — store, db, jobs (3)
- Trailing slash trimmed once, not repeatedly — queue, jobs (2)
- Trace id survives a retry — api (3)
- Token parser error messages are more specific — core, billing, queue (3)
- HTTP: timer cleared when the socket drops (`f66d359`), pool closed on shutdown (`eb874a5`) — these two are real leak fixes, worth their own lines
- `fix(db): stop logging the whole request body` (`1b55313`) — **request bodies were being written to logs.** This is a privacy fix and anyone with log retention should know about it. I'd call it out explicitly rather than bury it.

**Perf** (10 commits, all internal — I'd write one line, not ten): batched metric writes (queue, db), skipped JSON round-trips on hot paths (core ×2, store, db), removed redundant clones in mappers (api, store, billing), and `perf(api): reuse the parsed schema between requests` (`9f02d92`). No numbers in the log, so don't promise a percentage.

## Things labelled "refactor" that are actually breaking

This is the part I'd push back on before you cut. Four items are filed as refactors but change what users can see:

1. **`refactor(api): drop the unused v1 export route`** (`56dc828`) — touches `router.js`, `handlers.js` and `api.test.js`. A route was deleted from the API. "Unused" is an internal-telemetry claim; if it's a published route, its removal is breaking and belongs under Breaking with the path named.
2. **`fix(auth): return 401 for an expired token instead of 403`** (`1d2bd55`) — correct behaviour, but any client branching on 403 breaks silently. This is a breaking change filed as a fix.
3. **`stop re-exporting the internal error types`** — 8 commits across core, db, jobs, auth, billing. If those types were reachable from the package entry point, `import { SomeError }` now fails. Somebody needs to check whether they were in the public surface.
4. **`use the right units in the latency histogram`** (`59402bc`, `1f2bc4e`) — metric values change magnitude. Dashboards and alert thresholds built on them will read wrong after upgrade. Operators need this in the notes.

Also worth resolving: 11 `delete the dead feature-flag branch` commits across 7 modules. If any of those flags was documented or settable, behaviour changed with no note.

## Two things I could not determine from the log

- **Minimum Node version.** There are 5 `docs: note the minimum node version`, 4 `chore: pin the node version in .nvmrc`, and 6 `ci: run the suite on node 22`. That pattern is consistent with either "we documented what was already true" or "we raised the floor." Check `engines` in `package.json` against 4.1 — if it moved, it's the headline Breaking entry.
- **Whether the v1 export route was public.** Determines if item 1 above is Breaking or omitted entirely.

## Draft

Dependency bumps: nothing but patch/minor on both runtime (pino, zod, pg, fastify, knex, ioredis, undici, nanoid, dotenv) and dev deps. No majors, no advisories referenced. Per your "only what someone installing would notice" rule, I left them out.

```markdown
## 4.2.0 — 2026-09-02

### Breaking
- An expired token now returns 401 instead of 403. Clients that branch on 403
  for expiry need to be updated.
- The latency histograms in `store` and `core` now report the correct units.
  Existing dashboards and alert thresholds on those metrics will need rescaling.
- The v1 export route has been removed.            <!-- CONFIRM it was public -->
- Internal error types are no longer re-exported.  <!-- CONFIRM they were reachable -->
- <!-- Minimum Node version, if engines actually moved. -->

### Added
- Failed webhook deliveries are retried with exponential backoff.
  <!-- name the config option + defaults from src/core/config.js -->

### Fixed
- Request bodies are no longer written to the logs.
- Paginating past the end no longer throws on a null cursor.
- A duplicate header is no longer sent on outbound requests.
- An empty allowlist is now treated as empty rather than raising.
- The trace id is preserved across a retry.
- The HTTP client no longer leaks a timer when the socket drops, and closes
  its pool on shutdown.
- Trailing slashes are trimmed once instead of repeatedly.
- Token parser errors say what actually failed.
```

The four `CONFIRM` markers are the only blockers — everything else is ready. Want me to write this into `CHANGELOG.md`?
